newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS - BCH, Rothschild in private banking deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - BCH, Rothschild in private banking deal.

text.p: Spain's Central Hispano (BCH) bank (BCH) and British merchant bank Rothschild announced on Thursday a private banking deal that will raise BCH's European profile and broaden its Latin American business.

Internationally, the two will set up a portfolio and fund management joint venture in Geneva, with capital of three million Swiss francs ($2.1 million). In addition, BCH will invest $5 million to create a bank in Guernsey that Rothschild will administrate.

Domestically, Rothschild Asset Management will advise Banif, the private banking joint venture of BCH and Banco Comercial Portugues, on its international investments and in the development of new products for private banking clients.
Banif will advise Rothschild on Spanish equities.
"We are very optimistic for global business, particularly in Latin America, which until now has not provided this type of business," Emilio Novela, Banif vice president, told reporters.
BCH, Spain's fourth-largest bank, estimated that funds under management in the global deal could grow to $1 billion in the year 2000.
At the end of 1996, Banif funds under management had reached 372.6 billion pesetas ($2.6 billion). Rothschild has some $30 billion under management globally.
"This accord moves us a year ahead in our private banking plans in Europe," Novela said. "It completes Banif's offerings and at the moment there is nothing else to do there."

But it is in Latin America where bankers see the greatest opportunities. As economies there steady, savings that were once converted into dollars and exported for management abroad are now looking for other opportunities.
BCH has invested some $487 million to become the biggest banker in Chile and take a stake in Mexico's Grupo Bital.
Through Banco O'Higgins Central Hispano (OHCH), it also owns a network of banks in southern South America.
"This is the design of private banking (accords)," Novela said. "Now there is the capacity to make agreements with all our banks in Latin America except Chile."
Shares in BCH rose 10 pesetas, or 0.18 percent to 5,460, largely in line with the market, while analysts welcomed the deal.

"It is good and positive although not overly transcendental in its impact on volume," said Ignacio Cornejo, analyst at Beta Capital in Madrid. "But it is good to have ties with solid names with good franchises." ($ = 1.441 Swiss Francs) ($ = 145.9 Spanish Pesetas)
